title: Employment Situation, December 2026 (BLS, 08:30 ET) — the jobs print that lands the morning after the January coupon announcement and before the block auctions
source: EST: derived from BLS's own published scheduling rule — the Employment Situation is released on the third Friday following the end of the reference week (the Sun-Sat week containing the 12th) — plus the holiday-slip precedent this research established from BLS's own archive filenames. The rule was RE-IMPLEMENTED FROM SCRATCH and re-validated by this event's own never-assessed research on 2026-09-09: 5 for 5 against this calendar's confirmed entries (jobs-2026-09-04, jobs-2026-10-02, jobs-2026-11-06, jobs-2026-12-04) and the sibling-derived jobs-2027-07-02. FOR THE DECEMBER 2026 REFERENCE MONTH THE RULE OUTPUTS A FEDERAL HOLIDAY: 2026-12-12 is a Saturday, so the reference week ends 12-12 and the third Friday after it is 2027-01-01, New Year's Day. Every prior structural twin — the only years since 1998 where December 12 falls on a Saturday and the rule therefore returns January 1 — slipped EXACTLY ONE WEEK to January 8, 3 for 3, evidenced by BLS's own archive filenames which encode the release date: news.release/archives/empsit_01082010.pdf (December 2009), empsit_01082016.pdf (December 2015) and empsit_01082021.pdf (December 2020). Hence 2027-01-08, a Friday. The prefix is EST: and not BLS: because bls.gov 403s this runner: /schedule/news_release/2027_sched.htm, /schedule/news_release/empsit.htm, /schedule/news_release/cpi.htm, /bls/news-release/empsit.htm and the three archive PDFs above all returned HTTP 403 to curl under a browser user-agent on 2026-09-09, and WebFetch returned 404 on the 2027 schedule page — every one recorded in this proposer's probe-ref.blocked. The archive filenames were surfaced by web search, not fetched. BLS has not published a 2027 schedule at all as of this date. A derived date is not a published one. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-07, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED, NOT CANONICAL — and proposed because the calendar has a real GAP here, not merely an adjacency: tracked `jobs-*` entries run 2026-09-04, 2026-10-02, 2026-11-06, 2026-12-04 and then jump to 2027-05-07, so every Employment Situation from January to April 2027 is currently untracked. This is the first of them and the one inside the proposer's own corridor. WHY THE PROPOSER CARES: 2027-01-08 falls the morning AFTER the 2027-01-07 coupon announcement and the Friday BEFORE the block auctions (3-Year Monday 01-11, 10-Year Tuesday 01-12, 30-Year Wednesday 01-13). The announcement's numbers are set at the 2026-11-04 refunding and a jobs print cannot reach them, but it can and does reach the YIELD at which the block clears, which is the channel the auction ledgers own. HONEST LIMITS ON THE DATE, stated rather than glossed: the underlying rule is validated 5/5 but the January-1 slip is an inference from 3 historical twins, not from a published 2027 BLS schedule, which does not exist yet; BLS could in principle slip to a different Friday or shift the reference week. The date should be re-checked, and this proposal's status revisited, once bls.gov publishes its 2027 release schedule — normally in the autumn of the preceding year. Sibling lanes deriving BLS dates should note that bls.gov 403s the GitHub Actions runner entirely, which is the documented blind spot in docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md's honesty rules. `symbols: []` and `estimate`: nothing here licenses an entry.
